title: Adaptive Shrinkage with a Nonparametric Bayesian Lasso
text: R package bnplasso (developer’s version) implements Nonparametric Bayesian Lasso described Marin et al. (2025+). main routine package, bnplasso.lm(), returns object S3 class, "lmBayes", supported various methods print(), summary(), plot(), fitted(), residuals(), coef(), predict(), allowing users quickly visualize, evaluate, analyze output familiar fashion. function bnplasso.lm() can also implement Bayesian Lasso (Park Casella, 2008) Bayesian adaptive Lasso (Leng et al., 2014).

title: Adaptive Shrinkage with a Nonparametric Bayesian Lasso
text: First, let’s start loading packages required bnplasso necessary illustrative example. Next, let’s generate synthetic predictors. , training set size 250 (n.train), held-set size 2000 (n.test). covariate space 200 dimensions (p), covariate vector drawn multivariate normal distribution mean zero AR(1) covariance matrix, correlation parameter 0.7 (rho). Now, generate model parameters. , intercept term equal ten (mu), residual standard deviation one (sigma), vector regression coefficients generated way 10% entries nonzero (beta). Finally, let’s generate responses. can easily apply nonparametric Bayesian Lasso (Marin et al., 2025+) data function bnplasso.lm(). Note supplying design matrix response vector. user-supplied hyperparameters provided, bnplasso.lm() function attempt automatically determine appropriate values hyperparameters. said, different applications may require different tailored prior specifications. method summary() provides information model fit. includes details function call, well posterior mean, posterior standard deviation, various posterior quantiles, MCMC effective sample size model parameters. method plot() produces various model diagnostics plots, including posterior predictive checks residual diagnostics.   One can also extract individual chains containing posterior draws model parameters. instance, let’s extract plot chains intercept, beta_1, beta_200.    Note chains centered around true parameter values exhibit good mixing! useful class-specific methods include: can also visualize posterior co-clustering probabilities, .e., posterior probabilities two regression coefficients clustered together.  Note first 20 regression coefficients (nonzero) clustered together large probability, remaining 180 (zero) also clustered together large probability. , nonparametric Bayesian Lasso accurately performing variable selection. desired, one can also obtain point estimate partition regression coefficients. default, function get.partition() employs variation information loss function Wade Ghahramani (2018); however, users can also employ Binder loss function. One can visualize partition function coclust.point().  also possible perform --sample predictions using method predict(). result matrix size n.draws--n.test, column contains posterior predictive draws one points wish predict.  instance, plots show posterior predictive distribution along actual response values first last points held-set. Given held-set, one can evaluate --sample predictive performance model using expected log point-wise predictive density (elppd) function elppd(). held-set available, one can estimate model fit using functions psis.loo() widely.aic(), compute Pareto-smoothed importance sampling leave-one-information criterion (PSIS-LOO) Watanabe–Akaike information criterion (WAIC), Vehtari et al. (2017). Additional guidelines help pages using package functions available . Source code data reproduce results Marin et al. (2025+) available https://github.com/marinsantiago/bnplasso-examples.
code: library(mvtnorm) p <- 200 rho <- 0.7 n.train <- 250 n.test <- 2000  set.seed(1) Sigma.x <- rho^abs(matrix(1:p - 1, p, p, byrow = TRUE) - (1:p - 1)) X.train <- rmvnorm(n.train, rep(0, p), Sigma.x) X.test <- rmvnorm(n.test, rep(0, p), Sigma.x) mu <- 10 sigma <- 1 beta <- c(rep(5, 20), rep(0, 180)) set.seed(1) y.train <- mu + X.train %*% beta + rnorm(n.train, 0, sigma) y.test <- mu + X.test %*% beta + rnorm(n.test, 0, sigma) set.seed(1) out.bnp <- bnplasso::bnplasso.lm(X.train, y.train) summary(out.bnp) NONPARAMETRIC BAYESIAN LASSO   Call details:  a = 0.1 b = 4e-05 alpha = 0.4014365 n.obs = 250 n.preds = 200 n.draws = 5000 (after burn-in and thinning) elapsed = 11.53845 secs  Coefficients:             mean    sd   2.5%    25%    50%    75%  97.5%     n_eff Intercept 10.020 0.064  9.894  9.976 10.020 10.064 10.147 3802.6851 beta_1     4.931 0.086  4.767  4.873  4.929  4.990  5.103 5000.0000 beta_2     5.114 0.108  4.897  5.042  5.112  5.188  5.323 5000.0000 beta_3     5.003 0.111  4.790  4.928  5.004  5.077  5.216 3759.5150 beta_4     5.114 0.107  4.904  5.041  5.115  5.185  5.325 4162.1842 ⋮ plot(out.bnp) plot(out.bnp$post.mu, type = "l", ylab = "", main = "mu") plot(out.bnp$post.beta[,1], type = "l", ylab = "", main = "beta_1") plot(out.bnp$post.beta[,200], type = "l", ylab = "", main = "beta_200") print(out.bnp) fitted(out.bnp) residuals(out.bnp) coef(out.bnp) bnplasso::coclust.probs(out.bnp$post.clust_idx) part <- bnplasso::get.partition(out.bnp$post.clust_idx) bnplasso::coclust.point(part) pprd <- predict(out.bnp, X.test) dim(pprd) 5000 2000 plot(density(pprd[,1]), lwd = 3, xlab = "", ylab = "", "y_test.1") abline(v = y.test[1], col = 2, lwd = 3, lty = 2) legend("topright", c("Predicted", "Actual"), lwd = 3, col = 1:2, lty = 1:2)  plot(density(pprd[,2000]), lwd = 3, xlab = "", ylab = "", "y_test.2000") abline(v = y.test[2000], col = 2, lwd = 3, lty = 2) legend("topright", c("Predicted", "Actual"), lwd = 3, col = 1:2, lty = 1:2) bnplasso::elppd(out.bnp, X.test, y.test) -1.502845 bnplasso::psis.loo(out.bnp) bnplasso::widely.aic(out.bnp) 713.9746 712.7612

text: X matrix predictors dimension \(n\)--\(p\), \(n\) rows observation vector. y Response variable. numeric vector size \(n\). intercept Logical. TRUE, intercept term included model; otherwise, intercept integrated . TRUE, prior intercept non-informative prior form \(p(\mu)\propto 1\). Default TRUE. prior character string denoting type shrinkage prior employed. options either: () "bnp.lasso" implements nonparametric Bayesian Lasso Marin et al. (2025+), (b) "b.lasso" implements Bayesian Lasso Park Casella (2008), (c) "b.adapt.lasso" implements Bayesian adaptive Lasso Leng et al. (2014). Default "bnp.lasso". positive scalar. prior = "bnp.lasso", corresponds shape parameter gamma distribution used centering measure DP prior. prior = "b.lasso", corresponds shape parameter gamma distribution used prior shrinkage parameter, \(\lambda^{2}\). prior = "b.adapt.lasso", corresponds shape parameter gamma distribution used prior shrinkage parameters, \(\lambda_{j}^{2}\), \(j\\{1,\dots,p\}\). provided, function attempt determine appropriate value. b positive scalar. prior = "bnp.lasso", corresponds rate parameter gamma distribution used centering measure DP prior. prior = "b.lasso", corresponds rate parameter gamma distribution used prior shrinkage parameter, \(\lambda^{2}\). prior = "b.adapt.lasso", corresponds rate parameter gamma distribution used prior shrinkage parameters, \(\lambda_{j}^{2}\), \(j\\{1,\dots,p\}\). provided, function attempt determine appropriate value. alpha positive scalar. prior = "bnp.lasso", corresponds concentration parameter DP prior. prior = "b.lasso" prior = "b.adapt.lasso", argument ignored. provided, function attempt determine appropriate value. variance.prior.type character string denoting whether prior sampling variance independent-type prior conjugate-type prior. See Moran et al. (2019) details. options either "independent" "conjugate". provided, function attempt determine appropriate prior. max.iters positive integer corresponding total number MCMC iterations. Default 6000. burn.positive integer corresponding number draws discarded burn-. smaller max.iters. Default 1000. thin positive integer specifying period saving samples. Default 1. float Logical. TRUE, internal routines use single point precision improved computational efficiency expense numerical accuracy. FALSE, double point precision used. Default FALSE.

title: Expected log pointwise predictive density (elppd) — elppd
text: function computes expected log pointwise predictive density (elppd) object class lmBayes. Given test (held-) set, \(\{y_{\text{test},},\, \mathbf{x}_{\text{test},}\}_{=1}^{n_{\text{test}}}\), elppd defined $$\text{elppd} = \frac{1}{n_{\text{test}}}\sum_{=1}^{n_{\text{test}}} \log\left(\frac{1}{S}\sum_{s=1}^{S}p\left({y}_{\text{test}, } | \mathbf{x}_{\text{test}, }^{_{'}}\boldsymbol{\beta}_{(s)}, \sigma^{2}_{(s)}\right)\right),$$ \(p()\) likelihood observed data \(\boldsymbol{\beta}_{(s)}\) \(\sigma^{2}_{(s)}\) \(s\)-th draws coefficient vector sampling variance MCMC algorithm, respectively.
